liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Louie Louie** (1 review, 2 other sources): Reviewer found a Louie Louie played in Louisville the novel highlight of an otherwise fairly average show; Notes say this was the final performance of Louie Louie [4][6][11]
- **Big River** (2 reviews): Brent's fiddle-patch solo drew audible crowd reaction, even on the board tape; he was loud in the mix; Brent's fiery supercharged keyboard solo using the fiddle MIDI sound drew enthusiastic crowd response [14][20]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Sugaree as awesome [16]
- **It Must Have Been The Roses** (1 review): Show started slowly, but Jerry's lovely vocal work in Roses turned it around [20]
- **Foolish Heart** (1 review): Foolish Heart was still evolving and, oddly, came to an abrupt end [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **Louie Louie**: rare: 9 archived performances [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-04-09.147845.sbd.ultramatrix.miller.flac24** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 158 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1989-04-09.138255.kmr82i.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 158 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [4]. Said about its sound: Paused deck removed the encore break, so Knockin' starts abruptly; some digital noise in opening tuning fades before music [4]
- **gd89-04-09.nak.7858.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 161 min; rated 3.69/5 by 13 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer weighs soundboard against audience tape: board is clean with strong bass clarity, audience tape has ambiance and energy but less bass; Audience recording made with shotgun mics; instruments and vocals are clear, mics placed high to limit crowd noise, and it isn't sped up like the soundboard; Reviewer remembers the show as loud and says the audience recording sounds great [15][19][22]
- **gd1989-04-09.156412.OTS-Schoeps-PCM-Master-Mattes-Anon-Noel.t-flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 165 min [6]
- **gd89-04-09.sbd.miller.13207.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 146 min; rated 3.1/5 by 10 [8]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard recording good but slightly fast-sounding, especially in Uncle John's Band and The Other One; Reviewer says soundboard copy sounds too fast and recommends the audience tape instead [12][16]

## Around the show

- Reviewer sat in eighth row; describes the venue as an old all-wood barn with a stage looking about twelve feet high [16]
- Reviewer calls it perhaps an average 1989 show, yet one of the first to show off Brent's playing [14]
- Post-space songs matched the Greensboro show's, per the reviewer [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-04-09.147845.sbd.ultramatrix.miller.flac24**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [1]
- **gd1989-04-09.138255.kmr82i.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Craig Hillwig & Lenny Stubbe; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source: Neumann KMR-82i > DAT (48 khz); [4]
- **gd89-04-09.nak.7858.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jill and Rob R; source: 3 Nak CM 300's - 2 CP 4's (Shotguns) 1 CP3 ( Super Omni ) arranged in an X-Y patter [5]. Also: Reviewer describes the audience tape as shotgun-mic recorded in 1989 [19]
- **gd1989-04-09.156412.OTS-Schoeps-PCM-Master-Mattes-Anon-Noel.t-flac16**: taped by Master Audience PCM recorded by Ted Mattes; transferred by Transfer by Anon Edited & Mastered (Adobe Audition) by Joe Noel December 10, 2021; source: (OTS) Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics (ORTF) > Oade capacitor supply > Monster Cable ProLink > Sony pcm-f1 > Sony sl-2000 > PCM (Master) [6]. Also: Recording shared by Ted Mattes, transferred by Anon; Danny Thompson supplied the patch source [6]
- **gd89-04-09.sbd.miller.13207.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> CM> DAT> CD> EAC> SHN [8]
- Show was released via Dead Drops, newly mastered from the original DAT recordings [28]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Kirsten Michel: [1989-04-09 Freedom Hall, Louisville, KY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1989-04-09-freedom-hall-louisville-ky-usa/) [29]
